# Decisions log

Append-only. Newest at the bottom. Reversals are new entries that reference the original.
Format: date, id, decision, alternatives considered, reason.
From D-100 on, every entry carries its date after its number; the section headers date the earlier ones.
A claim not verified in the session carries [untested] or [inferred] inline and a line under "Open questions"
in the handoff file (docs/handoff/).

## 2026-09-20

**D-001 — Alpha-5 element sets come from derived re-encodings of CelesTrak OMM records, never from Space-Track bytes.**
Alternatives: (a) commit Space-Track TLEs; (b) encoding vectors only.
Reason: the Space-Track user agreement prohibits transferring its data to other entities without approval and a repository is a transfer; CelesTrak records re-encoded by a committed script are real data with a reproducible transformation. Derived files carry `provenance: derived` with source record and script recorded. The project owner may verify the encoder privately against their own Space-Track account; nothing from that check is committed. (Owner decision.)

**D-002 — Fetch the Starlink G15-27 post-deployment SupGP file first, store under `raw/`, gitignore it for now.**
Alternatives: skip 9-digit coverage; wait for the next launch.
Reason: it is the only current source of provider-issued 9-digit ids and the ids disappear at cataloguing. If nothing usable is in it, the 9-digit element-set case is omitted; no synthetic records. (Owner decision.)

**D-003 — Derived KVN syntax variants re-serialised from real records are allowed.**
Alternatives: omit; hand-write examples.
Reason: CCSDS-legal forms that CelesTrak happens not to emit (day-of-year epochs, no fractional seconds, `Z`, bracketed units) are exactly what breaks parsers; each derived file records the source record hash and the transformation. (Owner decision.)

**D-004 — Phase 2 fetch budget approved as proposed in docs/PLAN.md §3 (about 40 requests, each URL once, under ~20 MB).**
Reason: well inside CelesTrak's published limits (100 MB/day, 50 errors per 2 h); the two one-download-per-update groups (`active`, `starlink`) are not requested. (Owner decision.)

**D-005 — Repository initialised at `Code Files/gp-omm-conformance/`; private until after the independent audit.**
Reason: redistribution terms for CelesTrak data are not yet settled (see D-007 and RESEARCH.md §11). (Owner decision.)

**D-006 — CLAUDE.md written without the `---` delimiter lines that surrounded the supplied text.**
Alternatives: include them.
Reason: a leading `---` block is parsed as YAML front matter by many Markdown tools and would hide the policy; the delimiters read as quoting marks in the instruction, not as content. Reversible in one edit if wrong.

**D-007 — No personal contact details in the fetch User-Agent.**
Alternatives: include the owner's e-mail (as some earlier one-off documentation fetches did).
Reason: CelesTrak does not ask for identification, and sending an address in request headers to a third party is not something the owner asked for. The UA names the project and points at the repository README. `GPCONF_CONTACT` env var lets the owner opt in.

**D-008 — The fetch tool does not follow redirects and never retries.**
Alternatives: default urllib behaviour (follow 301/302).
Reason: CelesTrak counts 301s toward its error limit and says responses to 403/404 "will not change by repeating the request"; a redirect means the fetch list is wrong and should be fixed by a human.

**D-009 — One fetch-list entry may record a non-200 response as data: `gp.php?CATNR=100000&FORMAT=TLE`.**
Alternatives: stop the run on any non-200 (the rule for every other entry); skip the request.
Reason: the response to a TLE request for a 6-digit object is itself a migration fact worth recording, and CelesTrak documents that TLE output cannot carry such objects. One request, never repeated, whatever the status.

**D-010 — `gp-first.php` is queried for ISS (25544) only, not for Vanguard 1 (5), in the first pass.**
Alternatives: query both.
Reason: if the GP archive does not reach 1998 for the ISS it will not reach 1958 either; avoids a probable 404. A second, single request may follow once the ISS result is seen.

**D-011 — SATCAT "both sides of 70000" uses the largest id below 70000 actually present in `satcat.txt`, plus 25544 and 100000, via `records.php`; no 8xxxx SATCAT query.**
Alternatives: guess 69999; download `satcat.csv` as well.
Reason: analyst objects are not in the public SATCAT, 69999 may not exist as an object, and the legacy file already tells us the largest 5-digit id; avoids a 404 and a second multi-megabyte download.

## 2026-09-21

**D-012 — Nine-digit ids taken from the full Starlink SupGP file and one per-object query, after the G15-27 file proved to use 72000-series ids.**
Alternatives: give up on 9-digit coverage; download the whole Starlink SupGP set in all five formats (~10 MB).
Reason: the G15-27 post-deployment file (fetched first, per D-002) carries ids 72000/72001. One CSV download of `FILE=starlink` (1.8 MB, subject to the one-per-update rule, requested once) showed 27 ids in 799501621–799501647; a single object (799501621) was then fetched by `CATNR` in CSV/JSON/XML/KVN/TLE. Real provider data, seven requests in total.

**D-013 — The `last-30-days` TLE 404 was recorded by hand from the tool's log and the tool now saves unexpected non-200 bodies before stopping; TLE-format entries whose 404 is informative carry `allow_error`.**
Alternatives: re-request the URL to capture headers; drop the fixture.
Reason: CelesTrak says a 403/404 "is not going to change by repeating the request"; the body was printed verbatim by the tool, so nothing is lost except response headers, which the metadata file says are missing.

**D-014 — Legacy `satcat.txt` (9.4 MB) fetched once and kept out of git; Phase 3 commits an excerpt plus the full-file SHA-256 and derived facts.**
Alternatives: commit the whole file; also fetch `satcat.csv`.
Reason: its only role in the corpus is to show the <70000 cutoff, which the excerpt, hash and counts prove; `records.php` supplies the per-object CSV/JSON records.

**D-015 — Catalog number 69999 is present in the legacy file and in `records.php`, so it is the "largest 5-digit id" for the cutoff case (as D-011 anticipated).**

**D-016 — Derived Alpha-5 TLE lines will cover letters A and T only.**
Alternatives: invent ids for the other 22 letters.
Reason: the only real catalog numbers inside 100000–339999 are 100000–100789 (letter A) and the 270000–270449 Space Fence analyst objects (letter T). The remaining letters and the I/O skips are covered by the specification vectors (D-001). No fabricated ids.

**D-017 — `expected.json` records per-format expected values where the provider's renderings differ, instead of one canonical record per object (amends PLAN.md §2.2).**
Alternatives: one canonical record with tolerances.
Reason: the inventory shows the TLE rendering truncates eccentricity to 7 digits and BSTAR to 5 mantissa digits, and SupGP TLE epochs are rounded to the TLE's 864 µs resolution. A single expected record would assert a lossless round trip that the data contradicts; per-format values let a parser be judged against exactly what it read, and the case notes state which digits are lost.

**D-018 — New case `supgp-celestrak-classification-c`; all SupGP raw files remain gitignored until redistribution is settled.**
Alternatives: fold SupGP quirks into other cases.
Reason: SupGP records differ from GP in ways that break GP-only parsers (`CLASSIFICATION_TYPE` `C`, `ELEMENT_SET_NO` 0, extra `RMS`/`DATA_SOURCE` columns, 72000-series ids, reused `OBJECT_ID`), and their redistribution status is the weakest (RESEARCH §11.3).

**D-019 — CelesTrak's silence on redistribution is recorded as silence, not permission; publishing raw fixtures is deferred to the owner; building continues.**
Alternatives: treat "freely available" as a licence; stop work.
Reason: CLAUDE.md ("interpret licences and terms strictly") and the owner's instruction that this decides publication, not construction. Options are laid out in PLAN.md "Phase 2 amendments".

**D-020 — Phase 3 will validate CelesTrak XML against the OMM 2.0 schema set fetched from SANA by direct URL, and separately report validity against the current 3.0/4.0.0 set.**
Alternatives: validate only against 3.0 with the version attribute masked.
Reason: a HEAD request shows the 2.0.0 master schema still resolves at the URL CelesTrak declares (RESEARCH §12), so the document can be validated against what it claims to be, and forward-compatibility with the current standard can be reported as a separate finding.

**D-021 — Error budget transparency.** Five non-200 responses were received from celestrak.org across both phases: two from guessed documentation URLs during research (a lesson: find links on pages, do not guess), three deliberate one-time TLE-format probes kept as fixtures. All well under CelesTrak's 50-per-2-hours threshold. Some one-off documentation fetches in Phase 1 carried the owner's e-mail in the User-Agent; the fetch tool does not (D-007).

**D-022 — Clean re-capture of the three window-dependent TLE endpoints (owner instruction), one request each, at 2026-09-21T00:41Z.**
Result: `last-30-days` TLE again `HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found`, body `No GP data found`, now with the full header set; `analyst` and `DECAYING` TLE responses are byte-identical to the 00:11Z captures (same GP update window), so the 565→219 and 82→79 omission counts now rest on captures with full provenance. The hand-transcribed entry is kept, marked "original observation" and cross-linked as superseded for citation. The fetch tool now records the status line, every response header in order, the request headers and start/finish timestamps for every response. Re-captures are separate fetch-list entries with a `recapture_of` field; the duplicate-URL guard stays.

**D-023 — Corpus design (owner decision): no raw CelesTrak bytes are shipped. The public corpus is specification vectors, clearly labelled derived re-encodings, `expected.json`, SHA-256 checksums of the files we tested, and the fetch script that rebuilds `raw/` on the user's machine under CelesTrak's own terms.**
Consequence recorded here, not silently: checksums prove parity with what we tested **only for endpoints whose bytes are stable**. Live group queries (`GROUP=`, `SPECIAL=`, current `CATNR=`) change every GP update, so a user's re-fetch will not match our checksums and our exact expected values will not apply to their bytes. The design therefore has two tiers per case: **stable-source fixtures** (CelesTrak's `gp-first.php` first-ever records, SATCAT records, derived files, vectors) with frozen expected values verified by checksum, and **live-window checks** (structural and cross-format invariants that hold for any snapshot, plus our snapshot's values published as a dated reference). Stage F fetches the stable sources.

**D-024 — Stable sources chosen: `gp-first.php` for 25544 (1998 record, already partly fetched), 100000 (Saramago's first record), 270449 (a Space Fence analyst id, letter T), 81011 (an 8xxxx analyst id), and 69999 (largest 5-digit id).**
Alternatives: only live queries; more objects.
Reason: "first GP data available" for a given catalog number should not change over time, giving reproducible bytes; the set covers 19xx epoch year, 6-digit, both analyst blocks and the 70000 boundary in about 20 small requests. Stability is an assumption stated in the manifest; the checksum comparison in the fetch script will reveal any drift.

**D-025 — Raw provider files stay tracked in this private repository; the public release is a curated export into a fresh repository.**
Alternatives: remove raw files from git now; rewrite history before publishing.
Reason: the auditor needs the exact bytes we tested in one place; the Phase 2 commit already contains them, so a public push of this history is ruled out regardless. An allowlist-driven export (Phase 4) is simpler and verifiable. SupGP raw files remain gitignored per D-002.

**D-026 — `expected.json` carries per-format values only where the renderings differ, hoists constant per-set metadata out of the records, and omits whole TLE lines.**
Alternatives: one canonical record with tolerances (PLAN §2.2); full per-record metadata (1.5 MB for the analyst case).
Reason: D-017 as implemented; field substrings and parsed values are analysis, whole lines are the provider's bytes. Total expected.json size 2.9 MB for 16 cases.

**D-027 — A name longer than 24 characters is cut to 24 in derived TLE line 0 and reported as `object_name_truncated_to_24`, not as a value difference.**
Reason: the TLE format's line 0 is documented as a 24-character name; the only such name in the data (100465, 27 characters) belongs to a six-digit object, so the rule could not be checked against CelesTrak output; recorded in the provenance sidecar and the precision-loss case.

**D-028 — The TLE renderer used for derived lines rounds the BSTAR / second-derivative mantissa half up to five digits and truncates eccentricity to seven digits.**
Alternatives: truncate both (251/304 match); round both (257/304 on line 2).
Reason: only this combination reproduces all 304 CelesTrak TLE lines exactly; no document states either rule, so it is recorded as observed provider behaviour (ambiguity `ecc-truncation-vs-mantissa-rounding`) and as the named case `tle-vs-omm-precision-loss` (owner instruction).

**D-029 — Library failures found by the cross-check are recorded as library behaviour, not as corpus defects, and not worked around in the reference readers.**
Findings (python-sgp4 2.27, Skyfield 1.55): nine-digit ids cannot be initialised from OMM data; XML records with an empty OBJECT_ID raise TypeError; export_tle writes a zero second derivative as ' 00000-0' where CelesTrak writes ' 00000+0'. All three are exactly the kind of defect the corpus exists to expose; they go into the Phase 4 breakage catalogue and the per-case `library_findings`.

**D-030 — Both complete SANA schema sets (2.0.0 and 4.0.0, 14 files each) are vendored under `schemas/` with a SOURCE.md of URLs and hashes.**
Alternatives: only the OMM modules (fails: the master schemas include every message type).
Reason: validation must run offline and against exactly the files CelesTrak declares; the CCSDS documents are published for free use and are redistributed unmodified.

**D-031 — Derived KVN variants may fill header keywords with values describing the derived message itself (ORIGINATOR GP-OMM-CONFORMANCE-CORPUS, generation time, a MESSAGE_ID, a CLASSIFICATION text).**
Alternatives: keep all headers blank like CelesTrak.
Reason: CCSDS makes CREATION_DATE and ORIGINATOR mandatory and non-empty; a variant that exercises a compliant header needs real values, and the only truthful ones are ours. The provenance sidecar says so.

**D-032 — Specification vectors that go beyond the six official Space-Track examples (letter boundaries, skip boundaries) are derived arithmetically from the published table and labelled as such; invalid-input vectors state the reason.**
Reason: the table is normative; the boundaries follow from it; a reader can recompute them.

**D-033 — The SupGP snapshot values (one nine-digit record, the G15-27 stack and single nominals, the 27 nine-digit ids) are published in expected.json as a dated reference, flagged with ambiguity `supgp-redistribution` so the owner can strip them before release.**
Alternatives: omit all SupGP-derived values.
Reason: they are the only real nine-digit evidence and are analysis values, not raw bytes; the flag keeps the removal a one-line decision.

**D-034 — Two guessed documentation URLs earlier produced 404s; from Phase 2 on, every URL is taken from a page link or the provider's documentation, never guessed.** (Lesson recorded; see D-021.)

## 2026-09-21 (Phase 4)

**D-035 — `.gitignore` guard against Space-Track data, placed before any Space-Track account exists (owner instruction).**
Patterns match any path component containing space-track / space_track / space track / space.track / spacetrack in any letter case, plus directories of those names. Verified with `git check-ignore` on eleven sample paths (eight blocked, three unrelated names such as `spacecraft-tracking.md` not blocked). One speculative pattern for export-file names was written wrongly (`?` is "any one character" in gitignore, not "optional") and removed rather than kept broken. The export tool applies the same guard by regex.

**D-036 — The zero second-derivative exponent sign fully explains every `export_tle` byte mismatch: verified, not inferred.**
Against the 306 CelesTrak-served TLE/2LE records (recaptures excluded): 225 have a zero second derivative and 0 export byte-exactly, and in all 225 the only differing columns are 51 (`+` vs `-`) and 69 (checksum); flipping the sign and recomputing the checksum reproduces every line. The 81 records with a non-zero second derivative all export byte-exactly. Line 2 is byte-exact in all 306. The same holds for the 604 derived lines (591 mismatches, all explained). The upstream draft states these numbers.

**D-037 — Evidence-basis statements added to the precision-loss and derived-Alpha-5 cases (owner instruction): the rendering rule was derived empirically from 304 CelesTrak record pairs and is not documented in any specification we located; the renderer was validated only against sub-100000 output.**
The owner verifies the Alpha-5 encoder separately against Space-Track; no Space-Track data enters the repository and the public claim describes the verification, not the data.

**D-038 — Runner design: data-driven from `manifest.json` and `expected.json`, standard library only, Python 3.9+, duck-typed parser protocol (`parse(raw, fmt)` plus four optional vector hooks), external-command mode for non-Python parsers, and two oracles: frozen expected values when the file's SHA-256 matches the tested snapshot, otherwise the corpus's own reference reader applied to the user's bytes, labelled as such in every report line.**
Alternatives: require the user's parser to emit our exact JSON schema; skip live files entirely.
Reason: any parser in any language can be tested; the report never presents a reference-derived comparison as a human-verified one.

**D-039 — Tolerances for the parser under test: floats compared at 1e-12 relative, epochs within 2 microseconds; everything else exact. The oracle values themselves stay exact decimal strings.**
Alternatives: exact comparison of everything (python-sgp4 then failed on 1-microsecond Julian-date float noise and on 1e-16 unit-conversion noise, which is not a conformance defect); looser tolerances (would hide the 86-microsecond SupGP epoch quantisation, so the TLE/OMM epoch check keeps its own 432-microsecond rule).

**D-040 — Library findings are reported as failures of that adapter, never worked around: nine-digit ValueError, XML empty-OBJECT_ID TypeError, classification reset to 'U' by `sgp4init` after `omm.initialize`, lenient Alpha-5 decoding (I, O, lowercase, four characters accepted; negative encodes to '-0001'). The first three have upstream drafts in `docs/upstream/` (the fourth, minor, is noted in the third's sibling draft); the owner files them.**

**D-041 — LICENSE copyright line reads "Honorius Neogy", the name used as git author, which was inferred from the owner's e-mail address rather than stated. Flagged for the owner to confirm or change before publication.**

**D-042 — Ordinary users' `tools/fetch.py` runs skip the three maintainer-only re-capture entries (`--include-recaptures` restores them).**
Reason: they exist to document provenance of a window-dependent observation; a user re-requesting the same endpoint twice would waste CelesTrak's bandwidth for nothing.

**D-043 — Public release = `tools/export_public.py` over `PUBLIC_ALLOWLIST.txt` into a fresh directory that becomes a new repository; the tool refuses `fixtures/*/raw/` and any Space-Track-named path and writes an export manifest with hashes. Dry run: 131 files, 0 refused. This repository's history is never pushed (D-025).**

**D-044 — CI runs offline only (unit tests plus the three shipped cases with the reference and naive adapters, Python 3.9 and 3.12). Cases needing raw files report `skip` until `tools/fetch.py` has run locally; CI never fetches from CelesTrak.**
Reason: a fetch per push would multiply load on a shared, non-profit service for no evidentiary gain.

**D-045 — A fourth, minor upstream draft (classification dropped by `omm.initialize`) was added beyond the three requested, because it was found during Phase 4 and silently alters a field; the owner decides whether to file it.**

**D-046 — Correction to D-040's wording:** the fourth finding (classification reset by `sgp4init`) has its own draft, `docs/upstream/python-sgp4-omm-initialize-drops-classification.md`, not a note inside another draft. D-045 is accurate; D-040 is left as written per the append-only rule.

## 2026-09-21 (owner decisions after the Phase 4 report)

**D-047 — Copyright holder is NEOGY LLC (owner decision; the owner's instruction called this D-046, a number already used by the correction entry appended after the Phase 4 report, so it is recorded here as D-047). LICENSE updated; the README names Honorius Neogy (NEOGY LLC) as maintainer.** The personal name remains the one used as git author since Phase 1, which was inferred from the owner's address and not corrected by the owner when flagged (D-041).

**D-048 — Tolerances approved (D-039) with a reporting requirement (owner decision): every check now yields `exact` or `pass-tolerance` separately, and a `pass-tolerance` item carries per-field count, mean signed difference and maximum, so a systematic sub-tolerance bias is visible.**
Implementation: three-state comparison (`exact` / `tolerance` / `mismatch`) with signed differences; CLI table gains a `tol` column; the reference adapter must be exact and the test suite enforces it. The TLE-versus-OMM epoch rule (432 µs) is the provider's own quantisation and is reported as an observation on an exact pass, not as a parser tolerance; treating it as one made the reference adapter look tolerance-dependent, which was wrong.

**D-049 — SupGP-derived snapshot values are withheld from the public release (owner decision). Definition: the element values (epoch, mean motion, eccentricity, angles, BSTAR, first and second derivative) and raw TLE field substrings of CelesTrak supplemental records. Catalog numbers, object names and ids, counts, hashes, URLs and aggregate statistics are metadata and stay.**
Mechanics: `tools/public_scrub.py` (single definition), applied by `tools/export_public.py` on the way out (records of the two SupGP cases emptied and marked `records_withheld`; SupGP pair items removed from the two pairs cases, summaries kept), by `tools/make_failures.py` (value details withheld for those cases) and enforced by `tests/test_export.py`, which exports to a temporary directory and fails if any distinctive SupGP value string appears anywhere. `docs/INVENTORY.md` is dropped from the allowlist because it quotes SupGP field values. The runner falls back to the reference-reader oracle for the withheld cases and labels it. The leak test's distinctive set excludes four-decimal angles, seven-digit eccentricities and zero fields because identical values were found in unrelated GP records (false positives, verified), leaving epochs, mean motions and non-zero drag terms. The catalog-id text vectors gained a `parse_catalog_id` hook so nine-digit parsing is exercised without any SupGP element set.

**D-050 — export_tle report reproducer replaced (owner instruction) by an ordinary five-digit TLE: the CCSDS 502.0-B-3 annex G example rendered in CelesTrak's layout with a zero second derivative written `+0`; verified to differ from `export_tle` output at columns 51 and 69 only. One variable per report.**

**D-051 — Empty-OBJECT_ID report now offers a pull request; the patch is prepared, not submitted (owner instruction).**
`docs/upstream/patches/0001-omm-tolerate-empty-or-UNKNOWN-OBJECT_ID.patch`: `parse_xml` treats empty element text as `''`; `initialize` derives `intldesg` only from a `YYYY-NNNP...` value (empty and `UNKNOWN` give `''`; today `UNKNOWN` yields `'KNOWN'`); two tests in the style of `sgp4/tests.py`. Verified on a temporary copy of the installed package: applies cleanly; before the patch the test body raises `TypeError`; after it the new tests and all 47 functions of python-sgp4's own test module pass. Upstream sources for the diff were fetched from master (`omm.py` identical to the released 2.27). An earlier "before" check in the session used the wrong OBJECT_ID string and proved nothing; it was redone.

**D-052 — Next step is an independent audit in a fresh session (owner decision); this session stops after committing.**

**D-053 — Correction to D-049's last sentence: the leak test's distinctive set is epochs, mean motions and TLE epoch fields only. Five-digit drag terms were also removed after they matched unrelated objects' eccentricity and BSTAR strings (verified false positives in `analyst-objects`, `alpha5-tle-derived` and `bstar-and-derivative-forms`). The withholding definition (all SupGP element values) is unchanged; only what counts as proof of a leak is narrower.**

## 2026-09-21 (independent audit and its resolution)

**D-054 — Independent audit received (`AUDIT.md`, produced by a separate AI session with no access to the building context, instructed to trust nothing and recompute independently). Result: no wrong expected value (65,887 field comparisons, 60/60 sample); three critical documentation/tooling findings, eight major, a set of minor. Owner instruction: fix every finding, record each resolution here, annotate AUDIT.md without altering the auditor's text, then stop for review.**

**D-055 — C1 resolved by implementing the drift check, not by retracting the claim.** `tools/fetch.py` now has `manifest_sources`, `drift_report` and `print_drift`: after every run, and on demand with `--check-drift` (no fetching; exit code 2 if any stable source drifted), every file on disk is compared with the SHA-256 recorded in `manifest.json`; a stable-tier source whose bytes differ is printed as `DRIFT` with the consequence (frozen expected values no longer apply; gp-first stability assumption violated or snapshot out of date); live-tier differences are only counted. `tests/test_fetch_drift.py` covers match, live drift, stable drift, missing files, tier precedence and the real snapshot. README, `docs/PLAN.md` and the `gp-first-stability` ambiguity now describe the implemented behaviour. This supersedes the unimplemented promise in D-024 and resolves M5 (same defect, decision-log side).

**D-056 — C2 resolved: the float tolerance is now genuinely relative, |got − want| / max(|got|, |want|) ≤ 1e-12, with no floor. Exact zero on either side requires exact zero** (no relative scale exists for zero, and a parser that returns a tiny non-zero for a zero drag term is wrong, not approximately right). README table and D-039's wording corrected in the README. All three adapters re-run: reference still 16/16 exact; python-sgp4's case statuses and every item status are unchanged by the change (before/after report diff: none); FAILURES.md regenerated.

**D-057 — C3 resolved.** RESEARCH.md §13 corrected with a marked note (all 565 current analyst records carry the literal OBJECT_NAME `UNKNOWN`; 563 have an empty OBJECT_ID); the analyst case's coverage line and interpretation now say so explicitly and cannot be read as "real names".

**D-058 — M1 resolved.** The 24-character line-0 limit is now described as a rule of the CelesTrak format document, not an observed rendering behaviour: it occurs in none of the 304 provider pairs and only in one derived line (100465). Removed from the precision-loss interpretation's list of observed rules, added as a coverage gap, README case row corrected.

**D-059 — M2 resolved by test.** `tests/test_roundtrip.py` parses every TLE record present (CelesTrak-served, including re-captures, and the 604 derived lines: 1,208 records in 15 files), expresses it as OMM keyword text, renders it with the corpus rules and compares bytes: all 1,208 byte-exact. The claim "TLE → OMM → TLE round-trips" is kept and now cites the test.

**D-060 — M3 resolved.** README and the supgp case now state what primary sources support: the legacy range ends at 69999 (CelesTrak); 80000–89999 is the analyst range (Space-Track); other uses of the 70000–99999 block, including the 72000-series ids, rest on a secondary source and are labelled as such. "Pre-catalog" removed.

**D-061 — M4 resolved: reversal of D-014.** No excerpt of `satcat.txt` exists and none will: under D-023 (no raw provider bytes shipped) an excerpt of the legacy file would itself be raw provider bytes. What the excerpt was meant to prove (line count, id range 1–69999, contiguity, absence of ids ≥ 70000, the full-file SHA-256, parsed lines for 25544 and 69999) is in `fixtures/satcat-70000-cutoff/expected.json`, and the runner's data check recomputes the facts from the user's own fetch.

**D-062 — M6 resolved.** Final fetch-error tally: eight non-200 responses from celestrak.org across all phases — two guessed documentation URLs (Alpha-5.php, privacy.php; Phase 1) and six deliberate one-time TLE-format probes kept as fixtures (saramago.tle, last-30-days.tle and its owner-instructed re-capture, starlink-38381 TLE, saramago-first.tle, analyst-270449-first.tle). D-021's "five" was correct at the end of Phase 2 and stands as that phase's figure; RESEARCH.md §12 updated with a marked note.

**D-063 — M7 resolved.** The export_tle draft now says nine queries returned records (five further TLE-format requests returned HTTP 404); the record count 306 was and is correct.

**D-064 — M8 resolved.** The README's `docs/` row no longer lists INVENTORY.md (it is deliberately not exported, D-049); `docs/README-draft-ai-assistance.md` removed from the public allowlist (kept privately as the Phase 3 draft record).

**D-065 — Minor findings, all fixed.** Version unified to `0.1.0.dev0` (manifest `corpus_version`, README, pyproject, package). Fetch-list duplicate guard is case-insensitive; entries carrying `recapture_of` are the only permitted repeats. `--skip-case` added to `tools/fetch.py`; README fetch text corrected ("never re-fetches a file it already has unless `--force` and older than two hours"). "29 of 29" restated as 28 distinct records (29 file-records counting one object's CSV and XML). **D-070 — Owner's Space-Track verification run (2026-09-21) and what it changes.** The owner ran `tools/verify_against_spacetrack.py` and shared the tool's printed fields, verdicts, column numbers and summary (no element values, no lines; the agent never read the saved responses). Result: 44 records (21 current GP records 100000–100020, 21 for 270000–270020, the first historical record of 100000 and of 270449); summary `exact 0, same_epoch_differs 21, encoding_only 2, no_derived_line 21, invalid_field 0, line2_field_mismatch 0, out_of_range 0, defects 0`. Interpretation by TLE column layout: (a) the Alpha-5 encoding is corroborated by provider output for both letters that exist in real catalog numbers, A and T: every field decoded to the queried id and every line-2 field equalled line 1; (b) no line was byte-identical because of two rendering conventions, not encoding: Space-Track writes a zero second derivative as `00000-0` (column 51, with the checksum at 69) where CelesTrak writes `00000+0`; and Space-Track's line-2 eccentricity differs from CelesTrak's truncated rendering in its last one or two digits (columns 32–33, on 9 of 21 same-epoch records), consistent with rounding; (c) the first historical record of 100000 on Space-Track differs from CelesTrak's `gp-first` record at the same epoch in the international designator (columns 10–16) while line 2 is identical, so a CelesTrak "first record" may carry metadata updated after first publication; (d) 21 records had no derived counterpart (100001–100020 predate the 30-day snapshot; 270002 was not in the analyst group) and two matched by field only because Space-Track holds newer epochs. Consequences recorded: the precision-loss rule is now described as CelesTrak's rendering, not the TLE format's; the derived-Alpha-5 case's evidence basis and gap, the `ecc-truncation-vs-mantissa-rounding` and `gp-first-stability` ambiguities, and the README gap and tool paragraphs describe the verification; python-sgp4's `export_tle` sign convention is Space-Track's, which the upstream draft should say when filed (it already notes Space-Track was not checked by the project; the owner may add this observation). ## 2026-09-22 (writer-side cases, first commit)

**D-095 — Writer-side case `tle-writer-alpha5` (new kind `writer`), adapter hook `write_tle`, external `--write-cmd`; inputs are records already frozen in the corpus; the precision rule accepts either provider's convention; secondary fields are information only; version constants unchanged.**
Alternatives: (a) test writers only through the existing `alpha5_encode` vector hook; (b) compare written lines byte for byte with CelesTrak's rendering; (c) fetch new records for the case; (d) bump the version now.
Reason: the corpus tested readers only, while every newly catalogued object needs an Alpha-5 field and amateur tools generate TLEs for new launches (owner's brief, 2026-09-22). The hook mirrors `parse` (same record keys; raise to refuse); `CommandParser.write_tle` runs `--write-cmd` with one JSON record on stdin (exit 3 = unsupported, other non-zero = refused). Inputs: the 604 derived Alpha-5 records (603 distinct ids, letters A and T; 270449 is in two derived files), the first ISS record (1998 epoch, negative first derivative, non-zero second derivative, zero BSTAR), the first record of 69999 (negative BSTAR and first derivative) and of analyst 81011 (blank designator, empty OBJECT_ID): 606 records whose canonical values are already frozen in v0.1.0's expected files, so the case runs offline with no new CelesTrak request and no new raw bytes; each input records the frozen file it was copied from, the source file and its SHA-256. Checks: `tle-checksums-valid` (reused), `tle-writer-catalog-field` (strict: five digits, or one letter of the table plus four digits; both lines equal), `tle-writer-round-trip` (the lines read back by the reference reader equal the input at each field's resolution by truncation or by rounding half up, because CelesTrak truncates the eccentricity and Space-Track rounds it, D-070/D-071; the convention observed is reported per field; this is the format's resolution, not a tolerance, and the reference writer stays exact), `tle-writer-refuses-unencodable` (D-096), and two information-only items, `tle-writer-secondary-fields` (derivatives, element set, revolution, classification, designator, name, and the sign written for a zero second derivative) and `tle-writer-matches-provider-rendering`, because fitting tools regenerate those fields by design and a rendering under the other provider's convention is not a defect. Wording rule (owner instruction): a refusal for a number the TLE field cannot represent is described everywhere, including `docs/FAILURES.md`, as the correct output, never as a capability gap. Adapters: reference = `gpconf.tle.render` (CelesTrak conventions; 606 of 606 fields byte-identical to the provider or derived rendering); naive = the catalog number through an integer format (six digits and 70-character lines above 99999, never refuses); python-sgp4 = `omm.initialize` + `exporter.export_tle`. `tools/make_expected.py` now accepts case ids so the new file could be built without rewriting the sixteen frozen ones (none was rewritten; `tools/make_manifest.py` regenerated the other case.md files identically). Version constants stay at 0.1.0; the number is assigned at tag time after the site is updated (owner instruction: merge, leave unreleased, update the site, then tag; the site, the forum post and the Zenodo record all say sixteen cases).

**D-096 — Three synthetic-derived refusal inputs (owner approval 2026-09-22; PLAN.md §2.1 reserves this provenance for owner approval): the SARAMAGO first record with NORAD_CAT_ID replaced by 340000, 799501621 and -1, the values of `vectors/alpha5.json` `encode_unrepresentable`.**
Alternatives: refusal tested only through the `alpha5_encode` hook.
Reason: the failure that matters is at line level, where the vector hook cannot see it: an integer-formatted writer emits six digits in a 70-character line, and strf's helper emits a blank field (D-097). The elements are real, the id is a specification vector no catalogued object carries, and every such input says so and carries the source record's SHA-256. Observed: the reference writer refuses all three; the naive writer writes lines for all three (`34000` in a 70-character line, `79950` in 73, `-0001` in 69); python-sgp4 2.27 refuses 340000 and 799501621 in `omm.initialize` and writes `-0001` for -1 (`to_alpha5` has no lower bound, as `alpha5-encoding-vectors` already records), so its writer-case status is fail on that one id.

**D-097 — strf investigation record: what was tested, what was inferred, the settled reachability statement, and why there is no adapter. No bug is claimed for the rffit binary.**
Target: strf (https://github.com/cbassa/strf, GPL-3.0, HEAD 92d2425 of 2026-03-06), the writer behind satno2tle (https://github.com/hobisatelit/satno2tle, HEAD 538269b of 2026-06-14). Both were cloned into the session scratch directory, outside both repositories; no strf code entered this repository (GPL boundary; an adapter may only call the binary). Where strf writes: `format_tle` (rffit.c lines 111-149) writes the catalog field as `%5s` of the string returned by `number_to_alpha5` (satutl.c lines 45-58: the table character at index `number/10000`, 34 characters with I and O skipped, no range check), classification `U`, a zero first derivative, a zero second derivative with the `-` sign, ephemeris type 0, element set 0 and revolution 0; the eccentricity through `%07.0f` (rounded) and BSTAR through `%11.4e` (five digits, rounded); the checksum counts digits and `-` (lines 130-146); `print_tle` (lines 1853-1890) writes the name, the two lines and a `#` trailer with LF endings, on the `w` key (lines 902-907). Alpha-5 reading was added 2024-12-22 (c1eb772, d3f5ab0) and writing 2024-12-24 (dbc250f); strf's own tests cover decoding only. Build: the rffit binary needs PGPLOT, X11, GSL and gfortran, none present here; nothing was installed. Instead strf's unmodified `satutl.c` and `rffit.c` were compiled with clang in the scratch directory (`main` renamed by a macro, gnu89, an empty stub `cpgplot.h`, undefined symbols resolved lazily) and linked to a 40-line harness of the agent's own that calls the two functions directly. Tested at function level: 5→00005, 99999→99999, 100000→A0000, 109999→A9999, 110000→B0000, 179999→H9999, 180000→J0000, 229999→N9999, 230000→P0000, 270449→T0449, 339999→Z9999, all as the corpus vectors; the real SARAMAGO first record with 100000 gives two 69-character lines with valid checksums whose field decodes to 100000 in the corpus reader, differing from the corpus's CelesTrak-style line only at columns 40-42 (first derivative zeroed), 51 (`-0`) and 65-69 (element set, revolution, checksum); 270449 gives T0449 with the eccentricity rounded (0045560, where CelesTrak truncates to 0045559) and the BSTAR mantissa rounded (10753-3); 69999 keeps `-70517-5`; for 340000, 350000, 999999 and 799501621 the helper returns an empty string (first byte NUL: index 34 is the table's terminator; above 34 the read is past the array, undefined behaviour) and the lines carry five blank columns 3-7, still 69 characters with a valid checksum and exit 0; -1 gives `0-001`. Side observation outside the catalog-number scope: `%2d` of `ep_year-2000` writes ` 5` for 2005 and `-2` for 1998 in columns 19-20. Reachability (code trace plus a decoder harness; one answer): every copy of a parsed catalog entry into the orbit (rffit.c lines 169, 207, 232, 418, 856, 929) goes through `alpha5_to_number`, whose arithmetic caps the result at 33×10000+9999 = 339999 (harness: Z9999→339999, ZZZZZ→330000, I0000→0); the `-i` option (line 333) only selects such an entry (lines 411-420); the only route for a larger number into `format_tle` is the interactive `c` menu item 9 "Satellite ID" (line 769, `atoi` without a range check). Inferred, not run: rffit has no non-interactive write path (options `-d -c -i -s -g -m -F -h`; display hard-coded `/xs`; keys through `cpgband`), so an adapter would need an X display and keystroke injection, which is what satno2tle's auto.sh does with xterm and xdotool (lines 293-303); auto.sh line 212 passes the raw catalog-field text of TLE line 2 to `rffit -i`, which applies `atoi`, so an Alpha-5 field would become 0. Decision: no strf adapter (owner's rule: only if buildable and runnable here); the writer case exercises the reference, naive and python-sgp4 writers, and the case text describes strf's behaviour as function-level observations. A hardening note for upstream is a separate decision (later entry, draft to the owner first).

**D-098 — Writer-result wording, so that a failure confined to the synthetic refusal inputs cannot read as a general failure (owner instruction after commit 1).**
Alternatives: leave the status table's "fail (1 fail)" to speak for itself; list passing items for every case in `docs/FAILURES.md`.
Reason: python-sgp4's writer-case status is fail because of the synthetic -1 vector alone, while it passes all 606 real records and both real-range refusals; a reader of the status row or of the single listed failure could not tell. Changes, none of them to check semantics: the runner's writer details now open with what passed ("2 of 3 numbers the TLE catalog field cannot represent (synthetic inputs, D-096) correctly refused (340000, 799501621); written instead of refused: id -1 ..."; "3 of 606 catalog field(s) correct; ..."); for the writer case `docs/FAILURES.md` lists, under each adapter, the checks it passed with their record counts, and its reading guide says why; the python-sgp4 finding in the case document states the 606-of-606 result, both refusals and the single synthetic failure in so many words. The three adapters' statuses are unchanged; the failure catalogue's other sixteen cases are unchanged.

**D-099 — `python -m gpconf check-tle FILE... [--against RECORDS] [--json OUT]`: the writer checks applied to a TLE file a tool wrote (owner instruction: its own commit, because it is what strf and satno2tle users would run).**
Alternatives: adapters only, with documentation for tools that cannot be wrapped; a separate script under `tools/`.
Reason: rffit is interactive and cannot be driven by `write_tle` or `--write-cmd` (D-097), but the file it writes can be checked. Design: a subcommand of the runner over the same functions in `gpconf/writer.py` (no second implementation); records are extracted leniently, any `1 ` line followed by a `2 ` line whatever their lengths, so a 70-character line is reported rather than skipped, with the preceding line as the name unless it is blank, an element line or a `#` comment (rffit's trailer, satno2tle's added lines); the format checks (69 characters, checksums, a strict five-digit or Alpha-5 field identical on both lines) run on every record; a six- to nine-digit number in the catalog columns is named with the Alpha-5 form it should have had or, above 339999, with the statement that a refusal was the correct output; the round trip and the secondary-field report run only when `--against` supplies the source records (any format the reference reader knows), matched by catalog number, and a missing source record is said so rather than failed; the zero second-derivative sign is noted. Exit 1 on any failing record or when no record is found; `--json` writes the per-record results. Tests use a file in rffit's layout produced by the corpus renderer, a naive six-digit line, a nine-digit line and a blank-field line; no output of an external tool is shipped.

## 2026-09-23 (audit follow-up, Batch A: the corpus said pass where it should say fail)

**D-111 (2026-09-23) — Batch A is a patch release (0.2.1 when tagged), not a major one; and A1: the TLE epoch field rendered an exact midnight as `YYDDD.-8000000`, fixed with a regression test.** Versioning (owner asked for the agent's reading of the README rule): the rule makes "changed `expected.json` schema or check semantics" the major trigger, and check semantics means what a conforming parser must do. None of the five Batch A items changes that: a parser that parses every record, matches every id and reads unchanged input passes exactly as before; the items only stop crediting outcomes that were never meant to count as passes (zero records read, an unmatched id in `check-tle`, drifted stable input treated as live) and fix a renderer defect and a metadata error. No expected value, check text or schema changes; A4's tier correction touches provenance metadata, not a frozen value, so the freeze rule holds. The visible consequence, a run that passed vacuously and now fails, is what a fix looks like, and the changelog's `[Unreleased]` section lists the five under "Fixed". A1, the defect: `epoch_field` (`gpconf/tle.py`) built the fraction with `str(frac)[2:]`, and `Decimal(0).quantize(Decimal('0.00000001'))` prints as `0E-8`, so any exact-midnight epoch, including the carry from 23:59:59.999999 under half-up rounding, rendered as `-8000000`: a 69-character line with a valid checksum (the minus counts 1) that the reference reader rejects, and through `writer.round_trip` a correct writer was failed at every midnight epoch. Latent in the frozen data because no input lies within 4.32 ms of midnight, which is why the 304/304 render validation and the 1,208-record round trip never reached the branch. Fix: `format(frac, 'f')[2:]`. Tests (`tests/test_roundtrip.py`, `EpochFieldTests`, failing before the fix and passing after): exact midnight, one second after midnight (`.00001157`), the last microsecond of the day under half-up (carries to the next day) and truncation (`.99999999`), the year rollover, and a rendered midnight line read back by the reference reader. Note on inputs: the ISO epoch is parsed at microsecond resolution, so an eight-decimal second such as 23:59:59.99999999 is not an accepted input; the TLE field's 864 µs resolution makes microseconds sufficient. Checked for this entry: the four failing assertions before the fix, the five passing after, the reference run 17/17 exact, and the writer judge at a midnight epoch reporting no mismatch.

**D-112 (2026-09-23) — A2: `check-tle --against` fails a written record whose catalog number has no match in the source records; it used to pass with a note.** The audit's reproduction: `check-tle fixtures/analyst-objects/raw/analyst-81011-first.tle --against fixtures/six-digit-omm-saramago/raw/saramago-first.csv` printed `[pass]`, the note "no source record with id 81011 in the --against file; round trip not checked", and exited 0. On the satno2tle path that is the likely failure mode itself: `auto.sh` passes the catalog field's text to `rffit -i`, an Alpha-5 field becomes 0 through `atoi`, rffit prints "No elements found" and continues with its zero-initialised orbit (rffit.c line 40; D-097, reading complete, not run), and the written line carries `00000`; a user who then checked the file against the source records got a pass for a TLE about no object. Now (`gpconf/writer.py`, `check_record`): an unmatched id is a problem, so the record fails and the command exits 1; the detail says "no source record with id N in the --against file; the round trip cannot be checked", and for N = 0 adds "likely cause: 00000 is what rffit writes when its -i lookup found no elements and the orbit stayed zero-initialised, e.g. an Alpha-5 field passed through satno2tle", for N = 99999 "likely cause: 99999 is rffit's default catalog number". Both causes are stated as likely, since the rffit behaviour is established by reading its source, not by a run. Tests (`tests/test_writer.py`, `CheckTleTests`): a file of four rendered records (100000, 123456, 00000, 99999) checked against a source file holding only 100000 exits 1 with the matched record passing, the other three failing, the rffit cause named only for 0 and 99999; a file of matched records only still exits 0; the older test that asserted the note-and-pass behaviour now asserts the failure. Both were failing before the change (one error, one assertion) and pass after; the full suite passes (43 tests). `docs/WRITERS.md` says so. Checked for this entry: the reproduction's exit code measured directly (1 after the change) and the reference run, unchanged at 17 of 17.

**D-113 (2026-09-23) — A3: a source file the reference reader reads zero records from, where the manifest records some, now fails the case with a description of the file; it used to pass every per-file check on zero records.** The audit reproduced it on a scratch copy: `iss.tle` replaced by an HTML 403 body, a TLE cut off after line 1, an empty KVN variant and a BOM-prefixed one all left the case at `pass`, with `tle-checksums-valid` reporting "0 record(s), all checksums valid" and the derived-KVN checks "variant parsed", because the values item is only emitted when an oracle exists and the remaining checks count zero records as success. That is the state `tools/fetch.py` leaves behind after an unexpected HTTP response, so a user who hit a rate-limit page got a green run. Rule now (`gpconf/runner.py`, `load_source`, before the parser under test is called): if the source's recorded `record_count` is positive and the reference reader returns no records, the item `source-readable` fails with "reference reader found 0 of N expected records; the file is <size> bytes, starts with <first 48 bytes>; looks like: <guess>", the guess being any of: empty file, whitespace only, UTF-8 BOM prefix, HTML document, CelesTrak's empty-response text, a TLE line 1 without a line 2, CSV header only (`describe_bytes`); the source's state becomes `unreadable`, which every per-kind loop already treats like a parse error, so no vacuous check runs for that file. A second rule covers the reader itself: when the file's hash matches the tested snapshot and the reader's count differs from the recorded one, the same item fails as an internal inconsistency. Live-mode files (hash differs) with a non-zero count are not count-checked, since rolling windows change their record counts legitimately. Distinguished on purpose: the 16-byte "No GP data found" bodies of the 404 sources carry `record_count` 0 and `http_status` 404 and keep their `empty-404` state; a positive `record_count` is the trigger, never the count zero. Tests (`tests/test_source_reading.py`, failing before and passing after): the four reproductions through `load_source`, each asserting the state, the item, the size, the quoted first bytes and the guess words; the 404 body staying `empty-404` with no failure; a readable file staying `ok` and a live file with a different count staying `ok`; a snapshot file with a wrong recorded count failing as internal; and, through `Runner.run` on a scratch root holding the shipped `kvn-syntax-variants` case with its first variant emptied, the case status `fail` with exactly one `source-readable` item, no "variant parsed" item for that file and the other variants still passing. Checked for this entry: the full suite (48), the reference run 17 of 17 exact, and the naive and python-sgp4 runs unchanged at 14 and 7 failing cases, so no legitimately passing file changed status. The README describes the item where it explains the runner's statuses.

**D-114 (2026-09-23) — A4: the writer case's source files carry the tier the case that owns each file recorded, not a blanket "stable"; the two rolling group files are live again, and `tools/fetch.py --check-drift` counts 22 stable sources, not 24.** `build_writer` (`tools/make_expected.py`) listed every file its inputs came from with `source_entry(path, "stable", ...)`, because the inputs themselves are frozen records; but the files include `fixtures/analyst-objects/raw/analyst.csv` and `fixtures/tle-omits-six-digit-objects/raw/last-30-days.csv`, the group snapshots the derived Alpha-5 lines were rendered from, which their own cases record as live. `manifest_sources` in `tools/fetch.py` takes "stable" for a path if any case says so, so those two rolling queries became stable-tier in the manifest: the audit's `--check-drift` counted 24 stable sources where the corpus has 22, and the first user to run the fetch tool after those groups update (every two hours) would have been told two stable sources drifted. The "stable if any case says so" rule stays: it is right when no case mislabels a file, and the fix is at the label. Now `originating_tier(path, from_case)` returns the tier recorded for the path by the case the input came from, or, when that case does not list the file (a derived line's canonical source belongs to another case), by the case that owns the fixture folder; a path no case records is labelled live and reported as a PROBLEM. The frozen input records keep tier stable, as before: the records are frozen values, the files are not. Regenerated: `fixtures/tle-writer-alpha5/expected.json` (the two tiers and the generation stamp change, nothing else), `manifest.json`, `MANIFEST.md` and the case document. Tests: `ExpectedInputsTests.test_sources_keep_their_originating_tier` checks every writer source against the tiers the other cases record for the same path, excluding the case-level label "mixed", and pins the two group files as live and the records as stable; `RealManifestTiers` in `tests/test_fetch_drift.py` checks `manifest_sources` on the real manifest: the two files live, and 22 stable raw fixture files, the count the tracker site checks. Both fail against the pre-fix data (a `stable != live` assertion; 36 stable paths counted before the fixture-only restriction, since the shipped derived and vector files are stable too) and pass after. Checked for this entry: `--check-drift` on disk (61 files match, 22 stable, 39 live, no drift), the full suite (50), the reference run 17 of 17 exact, and the expected.json diff limited to the two tiers and the stamp.

**D-115 (2026-09-23) — A5: a stable-tier source whose bytes differ from the recorded SHA-256 is reported as drift, explicitly: a failing `stable-source-drift` item in the case output, a `drift` field in the JSON report, and a values item that says the frozen expected values were not applied and why.** Before, `load_source` set the mode to "live" for any hash mismatch regardless of tier, the reference reader silently became the oracle, and the only trace was an `info` item shown with `--verbose`; the audit reproduced it by changing one digit of a stable file and reading `[pass] values` in the table. The tier promise is that a stable source is frozen (README, Versioning), so changed bytes mean either that the provider altered a first-ever record, which the maintainer must learn, or that the user's file is corrupt; either way the case as published could not be executed, and a green table would hide it. Status `fail` for the drift item, deliberately: the case's status then says the run could not deliver what the case promises, while the parser's own verdict stays visible in the values item, which is still computed against the reference reader and labelled "frozen expected values not applied: the stable source drifted from the tested snapshot". Live-tier sources are unchanged: rolling windows are expected to differ and keep the "live bytes" label. The run footer lists every drifted file and points at `tools/fetch.py --check-drift`; `CaseResult.as_dict()` carries `drift` as path -> recorded and actual SHA-256, so the JSON report and `docs/FAILURES.md`, which is generated from it, would show a drift if one ever occurred. Tests (`tests/test_stable_drift.py`, on a scratch root holding the shipped `alpha5-tle-derived` case, whose four sources are stable-tier): an untouched copy passes with all four values items "match frozen expected values" and an empty `drift`; a copy with one mean-motion digit changed and the checksum recomputed fails with exactly one failing item, `stable-source-drift` on that file, its detail naming the tier, the mismatch, both hashes and the reference comparison, a `drift` entry with a 64-character actual hash different from the recorded one, that file's values item passing (the reference adapter agrees with the reference reader) with the not-applied label, and the other three files still exact against the frozen values. Both tests fail before the change (a missing `drift` key; status pass) and pass after. Checked for this entry: the full suite (52), the reference run 17 of 17 exact on the untouched corpus, and the on-disk drift check (0 stable drift), so no item appears on a clean checkout.

**D-116 (2026-09-23) — Batch C, corpus: a stale count, two footnotes and the dating of entries.** The ambiguity `mmdot-convention` in `tools/cases.py` said "(301/301 records)", the Phase 2 count, while the case and the README count 304 of 304 pairs; it now says 304/304, and `MANIFEST.md` and the five case documents that copy the text were regenerated. `MANIFEST.md`'s summary table now carries a footnote that its records column sums the record counts of a case's source files, since `analyst-objects` shows 567 (565 group records plus the two single-object first fetches) against the 565 the text elsewhere quotes. The 0.2.0 changelog entry keeps "drafted and not sent" as the state at release and gains a bracketed note that the strf note was filed after the release as cbassa/strf#88 (D-108), so the two statements no longer read as a contradiction. Dating: entries D-100 to D-109 carried no date and D-104 to D-110 sat under a 2026-09-22 heading although they record events of the 23rd (UTC dates of the commits that introduced them: D-100 to D-103 on 2026-09-22, D-104 onward on 2026-09-23); each now carries its date after its number in the form D-111 introduced, a "2026-09-23" heading precedes D-104, and the preamble says every entry from D-100 on carries its date. The corpus handoff, whose filename carries the date it was first written, says at the top that it is the living handoff. No expected value, check text or schema changes. Checked for this entry: the regenerated manifest and case documents contain no "301/301"; the full suite; the export verified from a fresh copy.

## 2026-09-23 (audit follow-up, Batch D: runner and reader robustness)

**D-117 (2026-09-23) — D1: the reference readers reject malformed input with a clear error instead of returning a wrong record; `from_alpha5` follows Space-Track's definition strictly.** Audit item 10.9 found the readers silent on five inputs: a UTF-8 BOM (the CSV lost its first column name, the KVN read zero messages, a 2LE lost its first record), an XML document with a default namespace (one record with every field None, because the `find` paths are not namespace-qualified), a repeated keyword in one KVN message (last value won), a TLE epoch day of 000 or 367 (landed in the previous or next year), and `from_alpha5` accepting `'A-001'`, `'A 000'` and `'+1234'` through `strip` and `int`. Each is now a `ValueError` naming the problem: `read_file` refuses a file that starts with a BOM, since the provider formats carry none; `read_xml_text` refuses a root element in a namespace, since the corpus reads the unqualified NDM/XML form only; `read_kvn_text` refuses a keyword repeated within a message; `tle_epoch_to_iso` requires the day of year to lie in 001..365, or 366 in a leap year; `from_alpha5` requires exactly five characters, a digit or an uppercase letter other than I and O first and four digits after, which is Space-Track's definition and what `writer.strict_catalog_field` and the reference adapter's hook already enforced around it. In the runner, `load_source` reports a `ValueError` from the reader as "reference reader rejected the file: …" rather than as an internal error; other exceptions keep the internal label. Checked before writing the fix: a scan of all 84 raw and derived files found none with a BOM, none with an XML default namespace, no repeated KVN keyword, no TLE day outside its year, and every catalog field already in the strict form, so no passing case changes; and the adapter counts before (naive 14 failing cases with 76 items, python-sgp4 7 with 20) equal the counts after, because the naive adapter uses `int()` and the python-sgp4 adapter uses that library's own decoder. Tests: `tests/test_malformed_input.py` pins each of the five behaviours, failing before the change (fifteen sub-failures) and passing after; the A3 test for a BOM-prefixed KVN file now expects the reader's rejection, the clearer of the two errors. Suite and reference run checked with exit codes.

**D-118 (2026-09-23) — D2, runner completeness: the three listed-but-unevaluated checks are evaluated; `--vectors-cmd` reaches `parse_catalog_id`; a raising hook fails its vector, not the case; `norm_epoch` accepts UTC offsets and a leap second; the JSON report names a `--write-cmd` parser; the failure catalogue withholds SupGP values for every value-carrying check; `ndot_field` rounds half up.** 10.8, implemented rather than removed: `leading-dot-decimals`, `bstar-implied-decimal-exponent` and `negative-bstar-and-ndot` were in the manifest and three case documents but emitted no item, so a reader saw them "pass" by omission; the case documents present them as distinct checks and each is a few lines, so `Runner.check_field_forms` now compares the fields each check names against the same oracle the values item uses (frozen values in snapshot mode, the reference reader otherwise): the OMM keywords written without a leading zero in the file's own text (found by `leading_dot_keywords`: `.00048259`, `-.15975118E-3`), the BSTAR and second-derivative fields of every TLE record, and the BSTAR and first-derivative fields of the records whose oracle value is negative. A file without the feature emits nothing, and a case with none at all reports `not-exercised`, like the nine-digit check. A sub-tolerance agreement counts as a pass with the count in the detail; the values item already carries the tolerance report. Counts before and after: naive 14 failing cases with 76 items, python-sgp4 7 with 20, unchanged, because both adapters' values already agreed on those fields where the new items apply and the naive failures in `bstar-and-derivative-forms` are parse failures on a different file. 10.11: `parse_catalog_id` joins the four ops the external command protocol dispatches, so `--vectors-cmd` parsers get the nine-digit text vectors instead of a skip; a command answer without `result` or `error`, or that is not JSON, is a `ValueError` naming it rather than a `KeyError`. 10.10: the `two_digit_year` loop calls the hook once per vector inside a try, so a raising hook fails that vector with the exception's name and the other items are still produced; before, the whole vectors case ended as "internal error in runner". 10.12: `norm_epoch` accepts a `[+-]HH:MM` offset (converted to UTC) and `:60` (mapped to `:59`, as `tests/adapters/reference.py` already does in its own epoch parsing), so a parser returning an aware `isoformat()` or the CCSDS leap-second form is no longer reported as "parser raised". 10.15: the JSON report's `parser` names the `--write-cmd` command; `tools/make_failures.py` gains `render(reps, generated_at)` for testing and withholds failing details for the checks that embed element values (`values`, `omm-formats-agree`, `tle-values-match-omm-within-tle-precision`, `mmdot-is-tle-field-value`, `tle-writer-round-trip` and the three above) on SupGP-sourced files, while a structural detail such as a parse exception stays readable; `ndot_field` quantises half up like every other rendered field (`0.000000125` → `.00000013`, was `.00000012` under the Decimal context's half-even), scanned across every record the renderer touches, the 1,208 records of the round-trip test (604 from the CelesTrak TLE/2LE files on disk, 604 derived Alpha-5 lines) and the 609 records of the writer case: no MEAN_MOTION_DOT value carries more than eight decimals (1,651 have exactly eight, 148 seven, 14 six, 4 none), so there are 0 exact ties at the eighth decimal and 0 lines render differently under half-up than under half-even. The change is unobservable in current inputs. It rests on the rendering rule the corpus established empirically for the BSTAR and second-derivative mantissas (D-028, D-071: 304 CelesTrak record pairs) and on consistency with every other rendered field, which already quantises half up; whether the provider itself rounds a tie half up is not backed by a provider document and is the coverage gap `tle-vs-omm-precision-loss` and the writer case already record ("no rounding tie … was observed") [untested]. CLAUDE.md gains the zsh note beside the exit-code rule. Tests: `tests/test_runner_completeness.py`, nine tests failing before and passing after, including a general one that every check a case lists appears among its items for the reference adapter; the listed-checks tests skip in the public clone, where the raw fixtures are absent. Suite and the three adapter runs checked with exit codes.

**D-119 (2026-09-23) — D3, check-tle and writer robustness: check-tle reports unpaired, indented and BOM-prefixed element lines instead of dropping them; a day-of-year source epoch round-trips; every written record is checked for column layout; the epoch-string vectors compare the instant; `tools/fetch.py` never re-requests a file that lacks its metadata, requests a re-capture only after its original and never a URL twice in a run, judges the two-hour rule by `retrieved_at`, and exits 2 on stable drift; negative tests for wrong values, tolerance boundaries and the command protocol.** 10.6: `extract_records` paired only `1 `/`2 ` lines that began at column 1, so an element line without its partner, an indented pair and a byte-order mark vanished and the file exited 0, or 1 as "nothing to check" without saying why. `writer.scan_lines` now returns the records (with the indentation and the BOM as problems on the record, the lines checked with the indentation removed) and the strays; `check_file` emits one failing entry per stray (`unpaired: true`) and the CLI prints and counts them. 10.7: `writer._iso` normalised nothing, so a `--against` record whose EPOCH was the day-of-year form (legal in CCSDS 7.5.10; the corpus's own KVN case declares it) raised an uncaught `ValueError` out of `tle.epoch_field`. The normaliser `tle.iso_epoch` (calendar and day-of-year forms, any fraction length quantised to microseconds, an optional Z, a `+HH:MM`/`-HH:MM` offset, second 60) now serves `epoch_field`, `runner.norm_epoch` (which delegates to it; D-118's inline code is replaced, same behaviour, same tests) and `writer._iso`; the round trip in `check_record` is wrapped so a source value the corpus cannot read is a problem on the record, not a crash. It lives in `gpconf/tle.py` because the reader imports the renderer and the runner imports both. 10.4: `writer.check_layout` pins every field of both lines to its columns (the decimal points at columns 24 and 35 of line 1 and 12, 21, 38, 47 and 55 of line 2, the separators, digits-only and right-justified fields); it runs in `check_record` and as the new writer item `tle-writer-column-layout`, added to `CHECKS` and to the case (expected.json, case.md, manifest and MANIFEST.md regenerated offline). The gap was real: the test builds a line 2 with a left-justified inclination and a recomputed checksum, and `check_lines`, `check_catalog_field` and `round_trip` all pass on it. Every provider and derived record the round-trip test renders (1,208) and python-sgp4's 606 exports have the standard layout. 10.5: `vectors/ccsds-epoch-strings.json` carries `iso`, the instant each valid string denotes (values computed by the reference adapter and checked against the calendar by hand: day 64 of 2020 is 4 March, day 204 of 2002 is 23 July), plus `iso_alternatives` for the leap second (23:59:59 or the next midnight, since a datetime cannot carry second 60); the runner compares the hook's result through `norm_epoch` within the 2 µs tolerance, so a hook returning a constant fails and names the vector. `ccsds-epoch-strings` joins `CHECKS` and the vectors case's list: the runner had emitted it since v0.1.0 but no manifest or case document described it. Counts before and after, over all cases: naive 14 failing cases with 76 items → 14 with 76; python-sgp4 7 with 20 → 7 with 20; reference 17 exact → 17 exact. The layout item passes for all three writers (naive's six-digit lines are 70 characters and fail the length check before any layout check; its three five-digit records are aligned); the epoch item is unchanged for naive (it already failed, rejecting five valid forms) and python-sgp4's adapter exposes no `parse_epoch`, so it still skips. 10.14: `fetch.py` gains `plan()` (what a run would do per entry, without the network), `run()` (the command line, parameterised by root, entries, clock and fetch function; `main` is `sys.exit(run())`), `duplicate_urls`, `read_meta` and `age_seconds`. A raw file on disk counts as fetched whether or not its metadata exists (before, a missing `.meta.json` caused a fresh request); `--force` reads the recorded `retrieved_at` and falls back to mtime only without metadata (a checkout or a sync rewrites mtimes); a re-capture entry is requested only with `--include-recaptures`, when its original is on disk, was retrieved at least two hours earlier and is not itself requested in the run (before, a fresh checkout with `--include-recaptures` fetched the same endpoint twice two seconds apart); no URL is requested twice in a run; the exit code is 2 when a stable-tier source drifted. Thirteen tests drive `plan` and `run` with a stub in place of `fetch_one` and a temporary root; no request is made. README and the script's docstring updated. 10.16: `tests/test_negative.py` shows a changed mean motion, catalog number and epoch are detected and named (an epoch off by 3 µs fails, by 2 µs passes within tolerance), pins the boundaries (2 µs inclusive, 432 µs for TLE epochs, 1e-12 relative for float-derived values, zero requires zero, exact decimals get no tolerance) and drives `CommandParser.parse` through `{fmt}` substitution, exit 3, a non-zero exit (the exit code and stderr are named), a JSON object instead of an array and output that is not JSON (now a `RuntimeError` naming it; before, a bare `JSONDecodeError`). The audit's last 10.16 sub-item, the naive must-fail test that passed vacuously in the public clone for the three cases whose CelesTrak files are absent (`six-digit-omm-saramago`, `analyst-objects`, `supgp-celestrak-classification-c`): the test is split. The four cases that ship with the repository are asserted unconditionally; for the three fetched-source cases the test asserts the failure where the files are present, asserts that a case without its files consists of `source-present` skips only (never a pass), and then reports itself skipped with the reason and the list of cases, so a reader of a public-clone run sees why. The alternative, driving the three cases from the frozen records, was not taken: the naive parser's failures there are parse failures on the provider's own bytes (six-digit ids, an empty OBJECT_ID, classification C), so rendering the frozen records back into CSV, JSON, XML, KVN and TLE would test the corpus's rendering rather than the provider's files, and the SupGP case's values are withheld from the export (D-049), so it could not be reconstructed at all; the decision policy prefers omitting to fabricating. Found while verifying the export as a fresh tree: a case none of whose files is on disk reported "not exercised" rather than "skip" when it listed a check with a case-level fallback item (`nine-digit-ids-parse` since v0.1.0 for `nine-digit-supgp-launch-nominals`; the three field-form checks of D-118 for `epoch-year-19xx`, `baseline-iss-five-formats` and `bstar-and-derivative-forms`), and the item's detail claimed the fetched data lacked the feature when nothing had been fetched. The fallbacks now fire only after at least one source was read; `tests/test_runner.py` `SourcelessCases` runs seven cases from a root holding only `manifest.json` and their `expected.json` and asserts every one is skipped with `source-present` items only (failing before the guard: `'not-exercised' != 'skip'`). In this checkout, where every source is present, the adapter counts do not change. Tests: `tests/test_check_tle_robustness.py` (16), `tests/test_fetch_requests.py` (13), `tests/test_negative.py` (19), all failing before the changes except where they pin existing behaviour; suite 114 under both Pythons, the three adapter runs and the catalogue regeneration checked with exit codes.

The audit statement in the README status paragraph, the README's audit bullet, the changelog and `CITATION.cff` says the independent audit covered v0.1.0 and that neither the writer-side case of v0.2.0 nor the Batch A–D fixes of v0.2.1 were separately audited; the audit of 2026-09-23 that produced the fixes is named as a read-only pass by a separate AI session under the maintainer's direction, not an independent audit. **D-121 (2026-09-23) — GitHub release v0.2.1 published at the owner's request ("Publish it."), from the app's built-in browser in the owner's own GitHub session: title "v0.2.1 — audit follow-up fixes", existing tag v0.2.1 at b1407a5, label Latest, not a pre-release, published 2026-09-23T21:09:22Z.** The body is `docs/handoff/release-notes-v0.2.1-draft.md` from its third line on (the first line is the title itself and would have rendered as a stray line; the owner saw this before publishing), with the five "How to run" commands wrapped in a `bash` fence at the owner's request so they render as one code block; the SHA-256 of the form's body matched the file's before publishing, so the published text and the private draft are identical. **D-122 (2026-09-23) — Batch E1, corpus documentation read as a stranger (audit section 5, every item).** README: the quick-start comment on the control run says the nine-digit case reports not-exercised outside a launch window; "18 SDS" is expanded to the 18th Space Defense Squadron at first use (README, the nine-digit case title, the SupGP interpretation); a third tier bullet defines `mixed` (the pairs, facts and XML-schema cases list files fetched for other cases, use them structurally, and drift is judged by the fetching case's tier, D-114) and says vector and derived files are never fetched; the adapter section counts five vector hooks and the example gains `parse_catalog_id`. Case documents (generated by `tools/make_manifest.py`): every case with `raw/` sources opens its Sources section with one sentence saying `tools/fetch.py` creates those files and the runner skips until then, and a case whose files all ship says so; the source table prints a real status and time for every row: an expected 404 names its body ("No GP data found", "No SupGP data found"), a derived file says it is shipped and when it was generated (from its provenance sidecar), a vector file says it is shipped and never fetched; a re-capture row carries a note naming its original and D-022 and stating that the `FORMAT` value is spelled in lower case (the reason for the spelling is not recorded; the entries are distinct through `recapture_of`, not through the spelling, since the duplicate guard is case-insensitive). **D-125 (2026-09-24) — Batch F (audit item 6): one synthetic-derived writer input with a positive-exponent BSTAR, under the D-096 precedent; letters B–S and U–Z stay vectors-only; the nine-digit re-capture is a standing item.** No fetched record carries a BSTAR with a positive exponent (the audit counted 1,206 TLE lines: 1,192 negative exponents, 14 `+0`, none ≥ 1.0), so the form `±NNNNN+E` with E ≥ 1 was untested. **D-131 (2026-09-24) — A catalog id the runner cannot take as an integer is reported in the values item, with the value and its type, instead of the runner raising inside the parse item (owner instruction after the satellite.js run).** Before: `norm_record` called `int()` on every integer field, so an adapter returning the raw TLE field `'A0000'` made the case's file fail with "parser raised ValueError: invalid literal for int() with base 10: 'A0000'", which reads as a crash in the adapter and hides what the library returned; the satellite.js adapter worked around it by returning no id. Now `as_integer()` converts what converts losslessly (an int, a digit string, an integral float or Decimal; a digit string still gets the type note that the `catalog-number-is-integer` check reports) and returns a problem text for the rest (a bool, anything `int()` refuses, a fractional float or Decimal); `norm_record` leaves such a field `None` and records the problem in the record's `_bad` map; `compare_values` reports "N record(s) whose norad_cat_id is not an integer, e.g. 'A0000' (str)" separately from records that simply carry no id, and "id X: rev_at_epoch is not an integer: 12.5 (float, fractional)" for the other integer fields; the integer check names up to three examples. `tle-catalog-field-decodes` is unchanged (a field with no integer is "not decoded"). Tests: `NonIntegerCatalogIdTests` (the conversion table, and the reference reader with the TLE field kept as text run on `alpha5-tle-derived`: no parse item, the values item names `'A0000' (str)`). Counts for the three adapters are unchanged (they return integers). Reason: several remaining Phase 2 candidates keep the field as a string (satellite.js, tle.js, the raw-string keepers), and the report must say what they returned.
